This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned V Addl.District and Sessions Judge and Add.Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in its judgment and award dated 01.10.2020, in M.V.C.No.944/2019.
2.

entities.text: V Addl.District and Sessions Judge and Add.Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the present appellant as claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 17.01.2019, while she along with other inmates were proceeding in a Car bearing registration No.KA-21-B-5634 and belonging to respondent No.1, towards Bengaluru from Belthangadi, at about 5.10 p.m., near Ragalli Bridge in Kunigal Bypass, National Highway-75, due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver, it dashed to a road divider and turtled, resulting in a road traffic accident.
In the said accident, she sustained multiple injuries and was admitted as an inpatient in Sanjivini Hospital, Hassan and took treatment for fifteen days.

Stating that at the time of t he Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
2 accident, she was working in a private company and was earning a sum of `20,000/- per month,
however, due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has become permanently disabled and as such, has lost her income, has claimed compensation of a sum of `15 lakhs from respondent Nos.1 and 2 before the Tribunal arraying them as the owner and insurer of the motorcar respectively.

sentences.text: 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their statement of objections.
Both the respondents have denied the manner of occurrence of the accident and the injuries alleged to have been suffered by the claimant and also the alleged permanent disability.
The insurer also denied the medical expenses said to have been incurred by the claimant and denied its liability to pay compensation.
Before the Tribunal, the claimant got herself examined as PW-1 and also examined one Dr.Deepak S., as PW-4 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-25.
On behalf of the respondents, neither any witness was examined nor any documents were produced.

4. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:
Sl.
 Particulars Amount in `
 No.
 1 Pain and suffering 15,000/-
 2 Medical expenses 51,000/-

3 Loss of earning during laid up period 4,500/-
 4 Attendant charges 3,000/-
 5 Food and nourishment charges 4,000/-
 6 Loss of future earnings 1,38,000/-

The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `2,15,500/- with interest at `9%
per annum thereupon from the date of petition till the date of realisation, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Insurer to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
3 6.
The respondent No.2 herein (insurer) is represented by its counsel.

Notice to respondent No.1 is dispensed with vide Court order dated 27.02.2023.
7.
Though this appeal is posted for admission, with the consent from both parties, the matter was taken up for arguments on main on merits.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that, he has the certified copies of the pleadings,
depositions and exhibits, as such, summoning of the Trial Court records is also not required and that he would place those certified copies before the Court.
With this, he places the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits for a perusal and their return to him.
8. In the light of the above, heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

Perused the materials placed before this Court,
including memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits placed before the Court by the learned counsel for the appellant.

9. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and respondent No.2 (insurer) having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.

Further, the claimant who got herself examined as PW-1, joined by two other claimants in the connected Motor Vehicle Cases, who were also examined as PW-2 and PW-3 respectively, have uniformly stated about the occurrence of the accident on the same lines as contended by the claimant in her claim petition.

In support of their contention, from the claimants side, the documents from Exs.P-1 to P-25 were got produced, which inter alia includes copies of FIR,
complaint, scene of offence panchanama, seizure mahazar, wound certificate, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report, charge sheet and discharge summary.

The evidence of PW-1 that the road traffic accident as alleged by her has occurred in the manner as contended in the claim petition due to the sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the motorcar is further corroborated with the FIR, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report and the charge sheet.
The charge sheet at Ex.P-7 accuses the driver of the motorcar for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The wound certificate shows that the claimant had sustained multiple injuries in the road traffic accident.

As such, the occurrence of the road traffic accident and the present appellant sustaining injuries in the said road traffic accident and also of the fact that the said road traffic accident occurred at the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the motorcar bearing registration No.KA-21-B-5634,
stands established.

Therefore, the question of occurrence of accident and the alleged liability of the respondent-Insurance Company to pay compensation to the injured claimant for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident need not be re-analysed again.
As such, the only point that remains to be considered is about the quantification of the compensation, which according to the claimant/appellant is inadequate.

Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
4 10.

The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted only one point that the Tribunal has taken the notional income at a lower rate, as such, it was required to take notional income at `14,000/- per month.
Further, the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities and the quantum of compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is also on the lower side.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company in his argument submitted that the - 10 - quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal being reasonable and just compensation, the same does not warrant interference at the hands of this Court.

12. The claimant as PW-1 in her evidence has stated that in the road traffic accident, she sustained multiple injuries both on her upper limb and was treated as inpatient in Sanjivini Hospital, Hassan for six days.

She also stated that, she has suffered great pain and also the wound certificate marked at Ex.P-5 shows that the claimant had sustained injuries in the form of extensive abrasion covering 2/3rd of both right and left upper limbs.
The doctor has opined that the injury was simple in nature.

However, the discharge summary of Sanjivini Hospital Hassan, produced by the claimant at Ex.P-8 would go to show that she had degloving injury in the right and left forearm and skin grafting was done during the course of the treatment.
It also shows that she was inpatient in the hospital from 17.01.2019 to 22.01.2019 for a period of six days.

Though the Tribunal has treated this aspect,
- 11 - however, it awarded compensation of a sum of `15,000/- towards `pain and suffering'.

Considering the nature of the injury and number of days the claimant has spent in the hospital as inpatient and the nature of the treatment undergone by her, I am of the view that the quantum of compensation awarded under the head `pain and suffering' deserves to be enhanced by another sum of `15,000/-,
thus, making it to a total sum of `30,000/-
13.

Though the claimant has stated that she has incurred medical expenses of a sum of `2 lakhs,
however, she could able to produce the medical bills and receipts and marked it at Ex.P-9, the total amount of which comes to `50,764/- as such, the Tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of `51,000/-
towards medical expenses.

14. Even after noticing that the claimant was inpatient for six days and she must have taken rest for a period of fifteen days, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `4,500/- towards `loss of earning during laid up period'.
In the said process, the - 12 - Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at `9,000/- per month as notional income.

Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
5 15.
No doubt, the claimant who has stated in her evidence that she was working at Bakery in Bengaluru and was earning a sum of `20,000/- per month, has not produced anything to corroborate the same.

However, in the process of taking the notional income, the Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income prevailing for the relevant year 2019 and which has been accepted and implemented by large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in the State.
For the said relevant year, the notional income at` 14,000/- per month was being taken by large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in the State.
As such, when the notional income of the claimant is taken at `14,000/- per month, for fifteen days laid up period, the loss of income would come to `7,000/-.
Since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `4,500/-, the claimant is entitled for differential amount of `2,500/- under the said head.
Towards attendant charges, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `3,000/- and another sum of `4,000/- towards food and nourishment charges.

Considering the nature of injuries and the length of inpatient duration in the hospital, I am of the view that the said compensation deserves to be enhanced by a sum of `4,000/-, thus, making it to a total sum of `11,000/- under both those heads.
17. Due to the injuries suffered by her, the claimant might have deprived of enjoying the amenities in her life to some extent.
However, the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities.

Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the claimant is entitled for a sum of `10,000/- towards `loss of amenities'.
18.
The claimant as PW-1 has stated that due to the injuries suffered by her in the road traffic accident, she sustained permanent disability.

In support of her contention, she got examined one Dr.Deepak S., an - 14 - Orthopaedic Consultant in Sanjivini Co-operative Hospital at Hassan, as PW-4, who in his evidence has stated that, he has examined the injured and has assessed the disability, which according to him,
is 18% each to the right and left forearm.
It is after analysing his evidence in detail, the Tribunal has rightly quantified the disability to the whole body at 8%, which does not warrant any interference by this Court.
Undisputedly, the claimant was aged between 32 to 33 years as per her medical records as on the date of the accident.
As such, the appropriate multiplier applicable would be `16'.

Thus, towards `loss of future income', the quantification of compensation would be `14,000/- x 12 x 16 x 8/100 =
`2,15,040.
After deducting a sum of `1,38,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, for the differential amount of `77,040, the claimant is entitled under the said head.

19. Barring the above, the claimant/appellant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
6 - 15 - enhancement of compensation under any other heads.
Thus, in total the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation as below :

Sl.
 Particulars Amount in `
 No.
 1 Pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2 Medical expenses 51,000/-
 3 Loss of earning during laid up period 7,000/-
 4 Attendant charges, food and 11,000/-
 nourishment charges

5 Loss of amenities 10,000/-
 6 Loss of future earnings 2,15,040/-
 Total 3,24,040/-
Since the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `2,15,500/- only, the appellant/claimant is entitled for an enhancement of a sum of `1,08,540/- in addition to what is awarded by the Tribunal.
It is for this enhancement amount only, the present appeal deserves to be allowed.

20. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
- 16 - ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;
 [ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned V Addl.District and Sessions Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hassan, dated 01.10.2020, in M.V.C.No.944/2019, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `2,15,500/- is enhanced by a sum of `1,08,540/- (Rupees One Lakh Eight Smt. Ranjini vs Naveen Disoza on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131760924/
7 Thousand Five Hundred Fourty only), thus fixing the total compensation at `3,24,040/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Twentyfour Thousand and Fourty only).

Draw the modified award accordingly.
